name: Great and Always Better
definition: We often say Netflix sucks today compared to where we can be tomorrow. We need the self-awareness to understand what should be better, and the discipline and resilience to get there.

rows.situation: Work that is good enough to ship and not as good as it could be
rows.justRight: Ships what members need now, and names the specific thing that should be better next.
rows.over: Refuses to ship because tomorrow's version is always more deserving.

rows.situation: A weakness in your own work or in the team's
rows.under: Needs someone else to point at it, and even then you argue.
rows.justRight: You can see the gap yourself, and you say it before the postmortem does.
rows.over: Catalogs flaws so eagerly that the team cannot tell a real gap from taste.

rows.situation: A gap you have already named
rows.under: Names it and does not change the next cycle.
rows.justRight: Puts the improvement on the calendar and does the unglamorous work to get there.
rows.over: Opens five improvement efforts and finishes none.

rows.situation: The improvement is harder than the speech about it
rows.under: Drops it when it gets dull.
rows.justRight: Stays with it. Adjusts the method. Does not pretend the gap closed.
rows.over: Keeps the effort alive after the gap has closed, because the program has a team now.

rows.situation: A habit that used to be why you were good
rows.under: Defends it because it is the culture.
rows.justRight: Keeps it only if it still makes the work better, and retires it when it does not.
rows.over: Tears out a working habit because it is old.
